- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above peak for 3–5 days.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — increase forecast tail by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 10-day average.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model fails to adjust — apply “sentiment lag” correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model ignores sentiment volatility in early horizon (first 5 days) — use sentiment history to weight early forecast with 30% less confidence; apply sentiment smoothing for first 5 days.
